subject: Biotechnology
title: FDA Regulation of Biologics
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on FDA Regulation of Biologics.

hook.text: A new drug takes 10 years and $2.6 billion to reach patients — FDA regulation protects safety but delays innovation.

buildup.text: The FDA's CBER regulates biologics — vaccines, blood products, gene therapies, and cell-based treatments require clinical trials.

discovery.text: Phase I tests safety, Phase II tests efficacy, Phase III confirms both in large populations — each phase can take years.

twist.text: Accelerated approval lets drugs reach patients based on surrogate endpoints — faster access but with required post-market studies.

climax.text: Breakthrough therapy designation cuts development time — the FDA works closely with companies on the most promising treatments.

punchline.text: Protect patients, enable progress — FDA regulation balances safety with speed.

quiz.question: What is accelerated approval for biologics?
options: Skipping all clinical trials for urgent medical needs
Approval based on surrogate endpoints with required post-market studies to confirm actual clinical benefit
Automatic approval for any biologic that passes Phase I safety trials
